title: Prefix stencils: Proof strip
topics: Two pointers, windows and prefix sums
summary: For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.
descriptionMd:
A running account lets the stationery desk recover trailing totals without rereading the full tape. Neri rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement prefixStencilsProofStrip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Prefix range subtraction. For each index i, produce the sum from max(0,i-k+1) through i inclusive. These are trailing ranges that may be shorter than k near the left edge. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
